app_name: Let your AI agents paint big arrows, boxes and text on your screen

novelty.justification: The repo is 1 day old, is not a fork, and adds a lightweight JS library compared to similar tools with hundreds of stars, indicating an incremental improvement.

system_requirements.justification: Install succeeded in 10.7 seconds and the library is installable locally, though it lacks a PyPI package, suggesting a fairly simple setup.

current_relevance.justification: As a devtool-library enabling AI agents to draw UI overlays, it aligns with the current trend of integrating LLMs into interactive front‑ends.

differentiation.justification: With 124 stars it trails the leading react-annotation (408 stars) but is comparable to smaller alternatives, and the only benchmark (import_time_ms 0.38) lacks a reference for advantage.

community.justification: The project has 124 GitHub stars, a single contributor, and was updated today, indicating a modest but active community.

ease_of_use.justification: 0 of 2 tests passed (0%) and install succeeded, showing core functionality is not verified by the test suite.

documentation.justification: No data on wiki, GitHub Pages, or topic tags was provided, so a neutral score is assigned.

maturity.justification: Created 1 day ago, with 2 forks and 1 open issue, the project is in an early stage of maturity.

summary: This is a lightweight JavaScript library that lets AI agents draw arrows, boxes, and text overlays on the screen. It is built in JavaScript/TypeScript and can be added to web projects without needing an API key. It suits developers who want simple visual annotations for AI‑driven interfaces. The library installs quickly and runs locally, but its test suite shows 0 of 2 tests passing and community signals are modest.
